sentences.text:
Coram : Nitin W.
Sambre & R. N. Laddha, Jj Dated : 20th February, 2023 P.C.:
1.

Mr. Patil learned counsel for the respondent no.
2/complainant raised an objection as to the maintainability of the present application for quashing,
as according to him the discharge application moved by the applicant is pending before the Court
below and as such, it is not open for the applicant to pursue the remedy of quashing and discharge at
the same time.
2.
Mr. Gole, learned counsel for the applicant would urge that since discharge application is initiated in the year 2014 and it was not decided expeditiously, present application is taken out.
He would urge that, he would not press the discharge application 12.APL.845.2016.doc before the Court below in view of the present application for quashing.
3. The statement is accepted.

The discharge application moved by the applicant in the Court below,
in view of above statement, stands disposed of.
4. This application is for quashing of Crime No. 257 of 2013 wherein applicant is already charge-sheeted for an offence punishable u/s. 376 of IPC.

The case of the prosecution is based on the claim of respondent-victim that the applicant has established physical relationship under the Jai Kailash Vachhani vs The State Of Maharashtra And Anr on 20 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/88192350/
1 promise of marriage.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
5. The factum of promise of marriage is not disputed by the applicant as reflected from paragraph - M at page no. 17 of the application, which reads thus:
"M.
That the perusal of the conversation between the Applicant and Complainant further shows that neither any force was used by the Applicant nor any false promise was made by the Applicant.
The incident with tool place was with the consent of both the parties.

The same is also manifested in the conversation between the Applicant and Complainant after the alleged incident dated 24.06.2013"
6.

Mr. Gole, learned counsel for the applicant while trying to make out the case for quashing would urge that the fact about the complainant will not be able to live with the applicant in US 12.APL.845.2016.doc where he was serving and she will not be entitled for any service visa having regard to her qualification, the higher costs of education in US was well within her knowledge.

7. According to him, the fact that the alleged proposal of marriage between the applicant and the non-applicant/ complainant is in rough weather, which can be inferred from the mobile chats which the parties had even after the alleged incident of rape.

8. Further contentions of Mr. Gole are, similar allegations were made by the applicant against a party in Delhi and the complainant thereafter has consented for quashing as could be inferred from the order dated 29/04/2022 delivered by Delhi High Court in CRL.M.C. 365/2022.
9.
He would further urge that during the time respondent no. 2/ complainant was in contact with the applicant, she was also chatting with 3rd person by name Mr. Amit Shahani.
It is as such claimed that the complainant is in habit of involving people in an offences of similar nature and thereafter extracting money under the said pretext.

10. Drawing support from the judgment of the Apex Court in the matter of Pramod Suryahan Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra 12.APL.845.2016.doc & Anr. (Criminal Appeal No. 1165 of 2019) which is followed in an order dated 27/07/2022 by the Apex Court in the matter of Mandar Deepak Pawar vs. State of Maharashtra &
Anr. (Criminal Appeal No. 442 of 2022) it is claimed that the prosecution against the applicant is not sustainable.

12. He submits that such affidavit shall be filed in any case by 27/02/2023 as this application is pending since last more than 6 years.
